mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over the prior quarter is associated with a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return due to higher discount rates eroding expected equity cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2.5% in the prior quarter
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >70% of post-2.5% crossings, or FEDFUNDS volatility is below 0.5% for 6 months after the trigger.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment falls below 5% for two consecutive months, wage growth (PAYEMS) accelerates, boosting consumer purchasing power and driving a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth rate exceeds 0.3% monthly and UNRATE < 4% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 5% confidence interval of baseline returns when wage acceleration is absent or unemployment does not fall below 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) relative to GDP (INDPRO) indicates pent-up demand, which precedes a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1/INDPRO ratio increases by >2% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are negative despite the ratio increase, or the ratio reversal is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of over 10% in two consecutive months suggests supply-side constraints, which typically precede a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >10% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the contraction, or INDPRO recovers >5% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: When the 1-month CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 0.2% for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a negative 20-day forward return as investors anticipate rate hikes.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL inflation rate > 0.2% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the inflation spurt, or the S&P 500 outperforms the S&P 500 1-month futures by >1% during the period.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in unemployment (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return as market anticipates continued hiring and economic expansion.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses below 4% in a single month
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are flat or negative despite the unemployment drop, or the drop is followed by an immediate rise in inflationary pressures.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (HOUST) above 1% suggest resilient consumer demand, which is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by >1% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns underperform a 10% confidence interval around the mean of prior 60-day periods without sales acceleration.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in manufacturing activity (RSAFS) of over 5% for three months indicates structural supply-side weakness, which is linked to a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return in non-recession regimes.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls >5% for three consecutive months and GDP growth remains positive
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive during the supply weakness, or RSAFS recovers >3% in the following quarter.
